News.title: Terrifying moment tornado rips through city sending locals fleeing as super typhoon leaves several dead in China
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a violent tornado ripped through a Chinese city forcing residents to flee for their lives.

A super typhoon has gripped parts of the country, causing flash flooding that has left several people dead.





Shocking footage from the tornado that struck Ezhou, Hubei, shows locals running for cover as extreme winds of up to 160mph destroy everything in their path.

In one clip, a restaurant’s glass door is shattered as debris travelling at frightening speeds smashes into everything in its path.

Trees were torn from their roots and market stalls were left crumpled into a heap.

An aerial view of the city’s streets reveals an apocalyptic scene in the aftermath.



The wreckage covers every square foot of concrete and devastated locals can be seen scrambling to deal with the fallout.

Flooding has killed at least two people in the southern Chinese city of Nanning, officials said on Monday, as rivers and reservoirs swelled with the path of Typhoon Maysak.

Forecasters have warned that another super typhoon is also threatening the country’s eastern coast.

Typhoon Maysak lashed large swathes of Vietnam and China‘s southern island province of Hainan over the weekend.



It is expected to dump the water it sucked up along the South China Sea as it heads inland.

Floods have already affected around 55,000 people in Nanning, the capital of Guangxi, with water spilling over or breaking through barriers at three reservoirs, deputy mayor Wei Jiang said late on Monday.

Officials raised the city’s flood emergency response to its highest level, warning “extremely heavy rain” could make the situation worse and hamper rescue efforts.

In Guigang, around 170 miles away, floodwater transformed a major road into a vast lake, swallowing cars and sending muddy torrents crashing down a hillside into a construction site.



The Ministry of Water Resources said water levels at Guigang Hydrological Station had surged to 138ft by 12.30pm local time.

Further south in Fangchenggang, another video showed a small car being swept down a flooded street.

Water reached the steering wheel of a second vehicle as a man fought to stop his electric scooter from being dragged away by the current.

China is also bracing for Super Typhoon Bavi as the monster storm barrels across the Pacific towards Taiwan.

The US National Weather Service said Bavi was packing winds of up to 180mph as it swept past Guam, Tinian, Saipan and Rota on Monday.



Weather authorities said the typhoon is expected to bring strong winds and torrential rain to eastern China from Thursday.

China has faced a summer of extreme weather, and analysts say weather-related disasters wipe out tens of billions of dollars in economic activity every year as factories shut, cities flood and crops are destroyed.

Typhoon Maysak made landfall in the southern island province of Hainan on Friday, the first tropical cyclone to hit mainland China this year, before striking Vietnam on Sunday and moving towards Guangxi.

In the Vietnamese border town of Mong Cai, state media reported the storm tore roofs from buildings and brought down trees.

Forecasters have warned of more heavy rain across Guangxi, Guizhou and Hunan in the coming days.



Together, the three provinces are home to more than 150 million people.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

China’s state planner has released 100 million yuan (£11million) for relief efforts in Guangxi.

The finance ministry and emergency management authorities have provided a further 160 million yuan (£17.5m) to support flood and typhoon response work across six regions, including Guangxi.

News.title: Welfare-obsessed Labour’s cowardly leadership is to blame for Britain’s naked Defence Investment Plan
News.content:
Naked at Nato

WITHOUT a Defence Investment Plan worthy of the name, Sir Keir Starmer is walking naked into the Nato summit.

The PM still reckons he can sell it to world leaders increasingly angry at Britain’s failure to step up to the plate.





But he is likely to receive a lukewarm reception at best from European allies — and a blistering one from Donald Trump.

Starmer had the chance to secure his legacy with a mega ramping-up of defence spending. Instead, he and Chancellor Rachel Reeves engaged in pathetic penny-pinching.

It has left us at barely over half the five per cent of GDP spending agreed by Nato.

The faithful promise to make defence the number one priority has been broken, leaving our Armed Forces way behind where they need to be.

Europe and the US know this. So, too, does Putin.

Moscow is now constantly testing Britain’s resolve.

Russian jets brazenly dropping sea devices to track a Royal Navy aircraft carrier were intercepted by the RAF.

It’s not the global threats that have diminished.

Just Britain’s standing on the world stage — and the blame lies squarely with a welfare-obsessed Labour Party and its cowardly leadership.



Woke up call

THE terrible murder of Henry Nowak brought home just how badly police forces have lost their way.

There are countless brave cops doing brilliant work across the country every day. But Henry’s senseless death show how many rank and file officers have been badly led astray by their own bosses.

For years police chiefs obsessed with box-ticking woke agendas have brainwashed their own recruits.

Common sense has been thrown so far out of the window that a stabbed white teenager can end up dying on the floor in handcuffs.

That is why the police continue to face accusations of two-tier justice.



Chief constables will never regain public trust unless they realise their job is to serve and protect us all equally.

’66 and all that

HOW could England possibly top their greatest World Cup performance since 1966?

By going on to win the whole thing, of course. What a joy it was to see the Three Lions battle all odds in Mexico to stamp their name on the tournament and become genuine contenders.

After we conquered the Azteca, sleepless fans really can dream that England can go all the way.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Erling Haaland’s Norway are up next.



Just like another English hero Alfred the Great in 878AD, King Harry and St Jude can summon an ancient English spirit to well and truly see off the Vikings.

News.title: Man, 21, charged with murder after 22-year-old stabbed to death in Hounslow during late night attack
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KNIFE TRAGEDY Man, 21, charged with murder after 22-year-old stabbed to death in Hounslow during late night attack

A MAN has been charged with murder after a 22-year-old was stabbed to death in a late night attack.

Officers were called to the junction of Bath Road and Great Southwest Road in Hounslow on June 30 following reports of a stabbing.



Haruun Hassan was found with serious injuries and sadly pronounced dead at the scene.



Awap Halouf, 21, has been charged with murder and possession of a blade in a public place.

Met Police officers and medics from the London Ambulance Service arrived at the scene at around 1.47am.

Specialist officers were deployed to support Haruun’s family after his death.

A murder investigation was launched on Sunday and a man was arrested in Cardiff in connection to the stabbing.



Halouf, of Hambro Road, Lambeth, has been remanded into custody and will appear before Wimbledon Magistrates’ Court on July 7.

During the investigation,a 21-year-old woman was also arrested in Cardiff on suspicion of murder.

She has been bailed while enquiries continue.

News.title: Huge fire erupts at oil refinery after ‘old tanker set alight’ as black smoke fills the air & locals told to avoid area
News.content:
A HUGE fire has erupted at an oil refinery with black smoke pouring into the air and locals told to avoid the area.

Fire crews descended on the Impala Terminal in Milford Haven, South Wales this evening with residents urged to shut their doors and windows.





Huge plumes of black smoke can be seen billowing into the sky and has been spotted miles away from the scene.

Footage and images online show a black cloud sweeping over the region as the blaze raged on.

Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service said they were called at 5.11pm due to a fire involving a “decommissioned oil tank”.

One person is believed to have sustained minor injuries and is receiving “appropriate care”.

A major incident was declared but was later rescinded as emergency services remain at the site to manage the incident.

Police urged locals to avoid the area as they shut down roads but they have since reopened.

An Impala Terminals spokesperson said: “Impala Terminals confirms that an earlier confined fire involving a disused oil tank at its Milford Haven site is now out and the incident is declared over.

“All employees and contractors have been accounted for.



“The site has since reopened and normal operations have resumed.

The site used to be owned by Puma Energy until it was taken over in 2022 by Impala Terminals.

A spokesperson for Mid and West Fire Service said earlier: “Several Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service crews are currently responding to an incident at Robeston West in Milford Haven.

“Please avoid the area and find alternative routes for your journey to allow access for emergency services vehicles.

“Local residents are advised to keep windows and doors closed if there is thick smoke in the area.”



A spokesperson for Dyfed-Powys Police said: “Officers are responding to an incident at Robeston West in Milford Haven. We are working closely with our partners on the response.

‘Please avoid the area.

“Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service are advising local residents to keep windows and doors closed if there is thick smoke in the area. We will issue an update as soon as possible.”

News.title: Enfield drill rappers found guilty of murder after shooting teen dead on e-bike over argument on social media
News.content:
'LIFETIME OF PAIN' Enfield drill rappers found guilty of murder after shooting teen dead on e-bike over argument on social media

TWO drill rappers have been found guilty of murder after shooting a teenager in the head while chasing him down on an e-bike.

Police were called to Great Cambridge Road in Enfield following reports of a shooting and found Keanu Harker, 18, with gunshot wounds to his head and chest.





Following an extensive investigation, officers arrested Tayvon Etefia and Emmanuel Popoola, both 18, and discovered that the killing was motivated by a row over Snapchat.

In a heartbreaking tribute, Harker’s family said: “Our son had just turned 18 when these individuals decided to take his life.

“We have been left with a lifetime of pain and loss that can never be undone.”

After Met Police officers found Harker’s body at around 8.45pm on June 26, 2025, in the north London borough, the teen was rushed to hospital but sadly pronounced dead the same day.



Homicide detectives found that Keanu was shot while cycling his bicycle while being followed by two men on a Sur-ron e-bike.

Etefia, then 17, was the one controlling the e-bike while his passenger, Popoola, also then aged 17, was the gunman.

After shooting Harker, the pair sped off to a nearby park and dumped the e-bike, as well as their clothes and a machete, into a neighbouring garden.

The pair were picked up in a black Ford Focus, driven by Eliezer Mbaki, and driven away.



Two days after the killing, Popoola’s girlfriend Anais King bought a £269 one-way train ticket from him to travel from London St Pancras to Paris.

Etefia also got himself a train ticket leaving for Paris the day after Popoola.

With detectives tracking Etefia’s spending and noticing the train booking, they alerted British Transport Police, who boarded the train and arrested the teen two minutes before its departure.

As Popoola had arrived in the French capital, Met officers monitored his girlfriend who went to visit him at his apartment on August 3.

Working with the French police, Popoola was arrested by the Paris gendarmes and extradited to London on August 14.



During a six-week trial at the Old Bailey, jurors heard that gang members had bragged about the murder in drill rap videos.

The prosecutors also showed Snapchat group messages showing Popoola angered by comments Harker made about him not being able to buy data for his phone.

Popoola and Etefia were convicted on Monday of the murder of Harker and will be sentenced on Thursday and Friday.

Detective Chief Inspector Lucie Card said: “This is a tragic case that yet again demonstrates why our commitment to tackling serious violence is so important.

“Our painstaking investigation established that Keanu was murdered because his killers took offence to something that was said in a social media group chat.



“Rather than ignore the comments, Emmanuel Popoola armed himself with a pistol and with the help of Tayvon Etefia carried out a drive-by shooting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This was cowardly and disproportionate violence that has understandably shocked the community.

“We spent months building a comprehensive case against the killers and those who tried to help them, and I am pleased to have been able to secure justice for Keanu’s family.”

News.title: Killer confesses to murdering nurse wife & promises to lead cops to her remains after years of professing his innocence
News.content:
KILLER SPEAKS Killer confesses to murdering nurse wife & promises to lead cops to her remains after years of professing his innocence

A FRENCHMAN jailed for murdering his wife despite her body never being found has made a shocking confession from behind bars.

Cedric Jubillar, 38, was found guilty of killing wife Delphine at their home in southern France in December 2020.





Despite maintaining his innocence throughout the trial, he was sentenced to 30 years behind bars.

It has now been revealed Jubillar sent a letter to his lawyers admitting that he was responsible for his wife’s tragic death.

In a news conference on Monday, lawyer Pierre Debuisson said: “A few weeks ago he said to me, ‘I need to tell you the truth. It was me.'”

Jubillar allegedly told how he killed his wife “after yet another marital row”, and used his car to move the body.

The twisted killer has now promised to lead investigators to the place where he disposed of her remains.

An appeal against his sentence was set to start two months from now, but this may now be postponed, his lawyers said.



The authorities were first made aware of what happened at the height of the Covid Pandemic when Jubillar contacted police to report his wife had gone missing.

Delphine, who was 33 at the time, worked as a night nurse in a clinic not far from their home in Cagnac-les-Mines.

The couple had two young children, aged six and 18 months.

Their son Louis reported a violent quarrel on the night of her disappearance while a neighbour also reported hearing a commotion.

Authorities carried out extensive searches in the surrounding countryside but Delphine’s body was never found.



While this was going on, a criminal case was slowly being built against Jubillar.

In 2021, he was officially placed under investigation and detained.

Malika Chmani, the lawyer representing the two children, said: “We are relieved for the children. Now he needs to tell us where the body is.

“I think that is what is going to happen now. I hope so.”

She added that Louis had always been certain his dad was guilty.



Prior to Delphine’s tragic death, police say the couple endured a turbulent relationship.

Cedric reportedly smoked cannabis every day and barely held down a job.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The couple had reportedly discussed divorce, and Delphine had started a new relationship with a man she met over the internet.

Debuisson said he hoped Jubillar’s confession will allow their two children to “grieve and give Delphine a proper burial,” adding that he “clearly regrets” his actions.

News.title: James Bond boss Barbara Broccoli reveals ‘constant fear’ during eight-year stalker hell as man is detained indefinitely
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BARBARA'S TORMENT James Bond boss Barbara Broccoli reveals ‘constant fear’ during eight-year stalker hell as man is detained indefinitely

A STALKER left James Bond producer Barbara Broccoli living in constant fear during an eight-year reign of terror.

Daniel Wilson, 37, waged a relentlessly disturbing campaign against her with hundreds of sexual and threatening messages, a court heard.





He got into the 007 movie producer’s home in 2016, terrifying two of her friends who had to barricade themselves in a room until police arrived.

Wilson then breached his resulting restraining order twice by leaving a voicemail, singing, “I’ve got murder on my mind”, and posting a vile social media message.

He also smashed up seven vehicles with a hammer in 2023, after being released from a psychiatric ward.

Ms Broccoli, 66, said she now feared going to public events, such as film premieres.

She said: “He’s caused considerable anxiety and distress.

“It’s corrosive.

“He’s undermined my confidence and affected my wellbeing.

“I’m in constant fear, always on edge and looking over my shoulder.”



At Southwark crown court, South London, Wilson admitted stalking Ms Broccoli and two charges of breaching his order.

He appeared via video-link from HMP Wandsworth and yelled “lies” and “b******s”, before Judge Christopher Hehir warned him he would be muted.

Wilson met Ms Broccoli after befriending her son in sixth form, but became obsessed with her.

He delivered to her a bronze bust of her father, the late Bond producer Cubby Broccoli, then demanded money for it and for allegedly contributing to the script of Skyfall.

Judge Hehir yesterday ruled Wilson would be detained indefinitely in a psychiatric hospital, telling him: “You have profound mental issues.



“The impact of your behaviour on Barbara Broccoli has been great.”

Ms Broccoli sold control of the Bond franchise to Amazon last year.

There is no official word yet on who will replace Daniel Craig as 007.

News.title: When will Harry ever learn? Entitled Prince’s whining in row over Palace stay may prove last straw with him & King
News.content:
HE’S no longer a working royal but Prince Harry is certainly the monarchy’s biggest Drama Queen.

Because what an absolute farce this forthcoming UK trip has become.





In a classic case of he says/she says, Buckingham Palace and the diva’s respective press teams have spent the past 24 hours frantically briefing against one another.

Quite what the late (actual) Queen, a woman whose famous motto was “never complain, never explain”, would have made of this latest debacle one can only imagine.

Following weeks of frenetic speculation concerning Harry’s possible rapprochement with his estranged father, the latest twist came after the Duke of Sussex’s camp told journalists (ones they liked) that Harry had accepted a gracious invitation from his father to stay at the Palace.

Then, yesterday morning, a furious Bucky P counter-briefed, clarifying that Harry had, in fact, not formally accepted the invite in time.

The Palace requires a minimum notice period to ensure a guest can be hosted and staff from the Royal Household provided. But Harry, being quite clearly entitled, said “yes” after the deadline had elapsed.

A spokesperson for Prince Harry said they understood the offer to stay at the Palace had been “withdrawn” — a decision they described as “disappointing”.

What’s disappointing is that both Harry fans and royal traditionalists, many of whom are unhappy with Harry and Meghan’s betrayal of the Royal Family, had been united in their desire for meaningful reconciliation.

After all, this comes at arguably the most fractious time in royal history.





Never has support for the King and co been so divided.

Last week, we saw this in action when Queen Camilla posed for a photo beside JK Rowling on the final day of Pride Month.

Gen Z were quick to go on the rampage, accusing Camilla of betraying trans people and making a pointed political statement.

They were quick to flood the official royal Instagram with hundreds of trans flags, incandescent with rage.

(That their photo opp, in Scotland, was actually to help promote Camilla’s wonderful childhood reading initiatives seemingly went right over their collective heads).

This is the same generation who love Harry and view him as a modern-day hero for “speaking his truth”, and breaking free from the toxic Establishment.

In contrast, Boomers were delighted by the pic, seeing it as a common-sense nod to biological reality.

Whatever the truth, it once again sparked debate as to the future of the Royal Family: how they can exist with so many young people believing them to be outdated, and a burden on the taxpayer.

Not the PR stuff of dreams.

This, of course, comes against the backdrop of the Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor horror show.



Harry’s latest UK visit was already embroiled in controversy over his ongoing security battles, meaning he didn’t feel it was safe for wife Meghan and their two children, Archie and Lilibet, to come with.

The outcome of his latest unedifying newspaper court battle, this time against the Daily Mail group, is also being published today with concerns it could compromise Charles’s constitutional position.

It’s all just so terribly EastEnders with Received Pronunciation.

Harry will be doing lots of admirable good on this trip, including the promotion of his incredible Invictus Games.

And yet, here we are again, all this charity being dismantled by behind-the-scenes bickering and now a very public comeuppance.

Charles has given his petulant son a chance here, and if Harry blows it, he might not get another.

LOVING LIONS’ SPIRIT

FAIR play to this current bunch of Three Lions.

Previous England squads, who have played like they have had guns to their heads, are clearly a talented bunch with an unbreakable bond.

But what is most refreshing to see are their post-match interviews.



Gone is the media-trained rigidity of their predecessors and in is an all-new, less-robotic approach to TV appearances.

In the early hours of yesterday, then, we had captain Harry Kane losing his voice following a boisterous rendition of Wonderwall, and then man-of-the-tournament Jude Bellingham telling fans to “have another shot” and pull a sickie.

Win or lose, it’s this spirit which makes 2026 England so brilliant.

TAKING THE PIP

COULDN’T have put it any better.

Fat Tony, beloved DJ of the celebrity set, said in an interview: “ADHD has become the new pulled pork, it’s everywhere.”

It comes as the Department for Work and Pensions reports a dramatic rise in PIP claimants with a sharp increase for conditions including anxiety, stress and ADHD, making up to 39 per cent of cases.

As well as this, the number of middle-class families receiving the benefit has nearly doubled over the past four years. Almost 200,000 households with annual incomes exceeding £100,000 are now claimants.

Crucially, too, PIP does not require a doctor’s “fit note” and is awarded based on self-presentation.

If would-be PM Andy Burnham, so-called man of the people, really wants to effect change, I suggest he starts with clamping down on those taking advantage of this insane benefits loophole, one which deprives people who really DO need help.



GUZZLING NICOLA GETS TONGUES WAGGING

NICOLA STURGEON, poor soul, has also had something of a PR shocker.

And while, granted, she doesn’t always help herself in the publicity stakes, pictures taken last week of her mid-scoff weren’t, well, flattering.

Lolloping tongue, wine a-guzzled and inhaling her food like she had not eaten in a month, this was not the public comeback of dreams.

Oh, the ignominy! In fact, the only person relishing this latest pap set must be her ex-husband, Peter Murrell, who, days earlier, started his five-year stretch in HMP Dumfries.

Where, unlike his wife in jaunty West London, buckets of chilled Savvy B aren’t readily available.

GIVE IT A REST BITE

“CAMBRIDGE PHD graduate” Lee Andrews released a self-pitying statement over the weekend, claiming he was suffering with mental health issues following a deserved social media onslaught.



If Katie Price’s ludicrous conman husband thought he would garner some sympathy, he should think again.

Not least because the self-proclaimed multi-millionaire once again showed himself up for the fantasist he truly is.

“I’ve tried to laugh it off,” he wrote. “But there has been no let up and its [sic] now resulted in my mental health suffering. I am asking for some rest bite.”

Rest bite?

I think you mean, respite, you moron. Did “Cambridge” teach you nothing, pal?*

*This man did not go to Cambridge University.

MEME OF THE WEEK

News.title: Man, 21, charged with murder after fatal west London stabbing
News.content:
Man, 21, charged with murder after fatal west London stabbing

Awap Halouf, of Hambro Road, Lambeth, south London, was charged with murder in connection with an alleged incident in Hounslow, west London on Tuesday where Haruun Hassan, 22, died

View Image Haruun Hassan, 22, was fatally stabbed in Hounslow in the early hours of Tuesday morning (Image: BPM Media)

A 21-year-old man has been charged with murder after a fatal stabbing in west London last week, police have said.

Awap Halouf, of Hambro Road, Lambeth, south London, was arrested on suspicion of murder in Cardiff on Sunday.

The 21-year-old was later charged with murder and possession of a blade in a public place, the Metropolitan Police said.

The arrest comes after police and paramedics were called to reports of a stabbing at the junction of Bath Road and Great Southwest Road in Hounslow, west London at about 1.47am last Tuesday.

Cops attended the scene alongside the London Ambulance Service and found Haruun Hassan with serious injuries, the Met Police said.

Mr Hassan, 22, was pronounced dead at the scene despite the best efforts of paramedics, and an investigation was then launched, the force added.

Halouf has since been remanded into custody and will appear at Wimbledon Magistrates’ Court, south-west London, on Tuesday.

A 21-year-old woman was also arrested on suspicion of murder in Cardiff on Sunday, and has since been bailed pending further inquiries.

News.title: Erika Kirk flees courtroom in tears as cop describes how her husband was murdered
News.content:
Erika Kirk flees courtroom in tears as cop describes how her husband was murdered

Erika Kirk left the courtroom at the Fourth Judicial District Courthouse in Provo, Utah, today as a police officer gave evidence of the moment her husband conservative activist Charlie Kirk was shot

View 4 Images Erika Kirk was tearful in the court today (file photo) (Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

Charlie Kirk’s widow left a courtroom in tears on Monday as prosecutors began to say out their case against his alleged killer, Tyler Robinson.

Erika Kirk, who began crying before the hearing started today, left the room in tears as a police officer described how her husband and conservative activist Charlie was shot on September 10, 2025.

Today’s hearing took place as prosecutors began to lay out their case against Tyler Robinson, accused of firing the single shot that killed Charlie Kirk as he spoke at Utah Valley University in Orem, 40 miles (65 km) south of Salt Lake City.

During the week-long preliminary hearing prosecutors aim to convince District Court Judge Tony Graf that there is sufficient evidence against Robinson, 23, for him to be formally charged and a trial date set.

View 4 Images Charlie Kirk's parents Kathryn and Robert arrive at court for the preliminary hearing (Image: Charles McClintock Wilson/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Charlie Kirk's parents and his widow, Erika Kirk, attended the court session for the first time along with Donald Trump Jr. and far-right influencer Jack Posobiec. Robinson's parents were also in attendance for the preliminary hearing.

Kirk was widely credited with convincing swathes of young voters to back Trump in the 2024 presidential election through his movement Turning Point USA. A firm advocate for reducing gun safety laws, Kirk previously claimed “some gun deaths” were acceptable in order to protect second amendment rights. He was assassinated during a public debate while attempting to answer a question about mass shooting statistics.

Robinson faces seven criminal charges including aggravated murder and prosecutors have said they would seek the death penalty for the student electrician, who turned himself in to police the day after the shooting. Judge Graf is also expected to rule on whether the death penalty will be an option if there is a conviction.

The hearing marks the most significant presentation of evidence in the case so far. Television crews, photographers and writers were camped outside the Fourth Judicial District Courthouse in Provo, Utah, today while the hearing got underway.

The court heard testimony from law enforcement officials about how events unfolded on the day of the shooting.

View 4 Images Tributes to Charlie Kirk (Image: AP)

Kirk's mother, Kathryn Kirk, clutched a pocket-sized packet of tissues. She listened to the proceedings with her head bowed and eyes closed. Widow Erika Kirk had been leaning her head on the shoulder of a blonde woman sitting to her right. Erika Kirk left the courtroom as a police officer described how Charlie was shot.

Defendant Tyler Robinson sat quietly between his attorneys at the defence table, looking at the exhibits on a monitor and occasionally taking notes. He wore a grey suit, a pale pink shirt, and a tie, with his wrists shackled to a chain around his waist.

Charlie Kirk's family thanked supporters for their kindness and prayers ahead of Monday's preliminary hearing.

"Every court proceeding serves as a painful reminder of his death," Erika Kirk, his widow, said in a statement posted on X, "and the loss that has irrevocably impacted our lives and the lives of his children."

View 4 Images Tyler Robinson during a previous hearing in Utah court (Image: Rick Egan/The Salt Lake Tribune via AP, Pool)

She added that the public outpouring "has sustained us during the darkest days of our lives." The statement was posted on behalf of Kirk's parents, Robert and Kathryn, his widow and his sister Mary. "Out of respect for the judicial process, we will not be commenting further at this time," the brief statement said.

Erika Kirk forgave defendant Tyler Robinson during her husband's memorial service in September. "My husband, Charlie, he wanted to save young men, just like the one who took his life," she said as she struggled to hold back tears. "I forgive him because it was what Christ did. It is what Charlie would do," she added.

Erika Kirk took the helm of Turning Point USA, the influential conservative youth movement that her husband co-founded aged 18, shortly after her husband's death.

Over the rest of the week prosecutors are expected to show video that captures Robinson at Utah Valley University before and after Kirk was shot along with other evidence linking him to the alleged crime.

Prior to the hearing, the defence attempted to ban livestream coverage and photographs of the proceedings, arguing that they were being used to fuel sensational media coverage.

Article continues below

Erika Kirk, however, insisted that cameras be allowed in the courtroom for the sake of full transparency.

News.title: Housing benefit freeze warning as claimants face 'impossible situations'
News.content:
Housing benefit freeze warning as claimants face 'impossible situations'

Prime Minister-in-waiting Andy Burnham - who has promised the biggest council house building programme since the post-war era - has previously criticised the housing benefit freeze

View Image Andy Burnham - who has promised the biggest council house building programme since the post-war era - has previously criticised the freeze (Image: AP Photo/Alastair Grant)

A housing benefit freeze is pushing people into a vicious cycle of debt with claimants facing “impossible situations”, charities have warned.

‌



It comes as new research shows fewer than two in 100 properties (1.9%) listed in Britain are affordable to people on the benefit. This is down from 2.7% in the previous year, according to Zoopla and charities, including Crisis and Citizens Advice.

‌



They warned it is pushing cash-strapped households into debt, poverty and homelessness, with record numbers of families already in temporary accommodation.

‌



Local housing allowance (LHA) rates - which control the maximum amount of rental support people can get— have been frozen for most of the past decade. The organisations are now urging the government to unfreeze housing benefit or risk pushing more households into poverty and homelessness.

Andy Burnham - who has promised the biggest council house building programme since the post-war era - has previously criticised the freeze. The PM-in-waiting singled out the policy last week during his first major speech since Keir Starmer announced his resignation timetable.

He said the country was in a housing trap where “we are forced to chase rents in the private-rented sector through the benefits system”. He added: “When governments try to control these costs by freezing Local Housing Allowance, it makes families homeless and places unfunded pressures on councils when they have to pay for temporary accommodation.”

‌



Matt Downie, Chief Executive at Crisis, said: “Across Britain, people on low incomes are facing an impossible situation. With housing benefits frozen, more and more people are struggling to cover the cost of rent and essentials like food and bills – forcing them into a cycle of debt, poverty and homelessness.”

He added: “What’s more, the freeze puts unsustainable pressure on an already overworked system. With local authorities already under immense strain and temporary accommodation costs at an all-time high, without urgent change we will only see more people trapped in this vicious cycle.

“To bring rates of homelessness down we must have a welfare system that supports people on the lowest incomes.

‌



“It’s crucial that housing benefit is uprated to cover the cheapest third of rents so it can work as intended and so that no one is faced with the trauma of losing their home.”

Dame Clare Moriarty, Chief Executive of Citizens Advice, said: “Many families are already at breaking point, cutting spending back to the bone and still finding themselves unable to pay the rent or put food on the table.

“Every day our advisers are hearing from more and more people who have simply run out of options. While housing benefit remains frozen, rents are spiralling - meaning private renters are cutting back, going without, or falling deeper into debt.

Article continues below

“If the government is serious about turning the tide on the cost of living crisis, getting to grips with the soaring cost of housing is essential. Private renters are struggling to keep their heads above water - unfreezing housing benefit would throw them a vital lifeline.”

A Government spokeswoman said: “We're tackling rising rents and the housing shortage with our commitment to build 1.5 million homes – the biggest boost to social and affordable housing in a generation – and our efforts to turn the tide on poverty are making a real difference, as household incomes have risen 5 percent in real terms and food bank usage has fallen.

"But we know there is more to do. That is why we have launched the £1 billion Crisis and Resilience Fund, are raising the National Living Wage by up to £900 a year for a full-time worker, investing more than £1 billion in homelessness services, and are investing a record £39 billion in affordable and social housing.”

News.title: ‘As an amputee, I was blown away by how accessible the British Grand Prix was’
News.content:
‘As an amputee, I was blown away by how accessible the British Grand Prix was’

When Jim Britt lost his leg in a gardening accident, it changed his life overnight. But, he says, some events are geared up for those with a disability - and Silverstone is one of them

View 4 Images Jim eyes up the British Grand Prix at Silverstone from an accessible platform

I’ll admit it, I took having two legs for granted. I spent 75 years as an able bodied person, not giving it a second thought. So when I had to have my right leg amputated through the knee this January, after falling off a ladder while gardening, to say that it was a shock would be an understatement. Overnight I found myself in a wheelchair, and the difficulties that brings with it. You see, it turns out that we live in an incredibly inaccessible world… if you’re on wheels, rather than feet.

‌



So when I find something that makes it easy for me to enjoy - I have to shout about it. And the British Grand Prix at Silverstone was one of them. So how does it work? Let me explain.

‌



At the base of plenty of the grandstands, there is an accessible viewing platform. The Silverstone website is pretty good at telling you which ones have them. My daughter Hannah and I had a ticket for Wellington, which included entrance to a little garden area away from the crowds. I also had a parking pass, pre-booked and paid for, to make things easy on the day.

‌



View 4 Images Jim and his daughter Hannah, who accompanied him to Silverstone

Once on site, parking signs funnel you to the huge public car parks. The best for disability is car park 51, but 46 was good too, near the Abbey entrance. If you tell the attendants you’re disabled, there are spaces near the top saved - but be prepared to prove it with a disabled badge.

Once parked, the ground is flat enough to easily leave the car park, and from there onwards a selection of pavements provide flat ground for wheelchairs to traverse. There are dipped curbs everywhere, and if anywhere is blocked off by a railing, attendants are on hand to open them and let you though.

‌



When inside the Silverstone site itself, while there are plenty of inaccessible footbridges taking spectators from A to B, there are also lots of tunnels and ramps, as well as lots of marshals to guide you to where you need to be.

View 4 Images The Wellington enclosure had plenty of places to sit, stand or roll around

In a matter of minutes I was at the Wellington enclosure. There, a big screen stood in front of several lines of coloured deck chairs, a photo wall provided the backdrop for souvenir portraits, and a covered seating area allowed some shade. Live music entertained us all while we decided between chicken wraps and burgers for lunch, and there was a bar too. Importantly, there was a fully accessible disabled toilet, large enough for me to wheel my whole chair into.

‌



To watch the race itself, a ramp led us up to a roomy viewing platform. Attendants were on hand to help if we needed anything, and there was the option of chairs or bays depending on whether I wanted to stay in my wheelchair. As we settled into our spot ready for the race, we were asked if we were okay and if we needed anything - a nice touch.

Then it was time for the race! And what a race it was, with Lewis Hamilton fighting for the podium for 52 breathtaking laps. I had a fantastic view from my bay, and spent most of it standing up on my leg, holding onto the front bar. It was exhilarating, and emotional too - being at Silverstone was something I thought may not have been for me anymore. I’m pleased to report I was wrong.

View 4 Images The fully accessible wheel-in toilet in the Wellington enclosure

‌



When the race came to an end we retraced our steps, and made easy work of getting out of the circuit. Our kind parking attendant helped Hannah shove the wheelchair into the car and waved us off on our way home.

As we drove away, I was struck by how relaxed I felt - and had indeed felt all day long. Every single moment had been thought out and catered for. Silverstone was truly a place for all. Accessible with a capital A, and therefore a joy to visit.
