News.title: Jude Bellingham tells England fans to pull a sickie
News.content:
England are into the quarter-finals of the World Cup, where they will face Norway, after a heroic last-16 victory over Mexico.

Even Donald Trump, the United States president, paid tribute to England on what was a chaotic night in Mexico that featured an hour’s rain delay, five goals, a red card and midfielder Jordan Henderson being taken to hospital despite not playing.

Trump posted on social media “Harry Kane of England is a GREAT player!!!” following the full-time whistle, while the Prince of Wales said: “Well done England! Bring on the quarter-final!”

The result at the famous Azteca Stadium is one of the finest by an England team on foreign soil, and the game will go down as an all-time classic.

With pubs across the country packed after licensing laws were changed by Sir Keir Starmer, the Prime Minister, the game was delayed by an hour because of storms in Mexico City – but for those who stayed up it was certainly worth the wait.

Twice England led by two goals, but on both occasions Thomas Tuchel’s team allowed tournament co-hosts Mexico to reduce the deficit, and they were reliant on an extraordinary backs-to-the-wall defensive stand after Jarell Quansah was sent off early in the second half.

Jude Bellingham was superb, scoring twice in 98 seconds in the first half, only for Julián Quiñones to reduce the deficit three minutes before half-time.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham said: “Text your bosses and tell them you’re not coming in, as simple as that.”

England’s plight worsened when Quansah was correctly dismissed for a wild lunge, but they regained their two-goal lead thanks to a Kane penalty after Anthony Gordon had been upended by Mexico goalkeeper Raúl Rangel.

But there was more drama to follow, with Kane conceding a hotly contested penalty that was converted by Raúl Jiménez.

Tuchel rang the changes as England dropped deep, but they clung on to their slender advantage.

Tuchel’s team will now face Norway, who knocked out Brazil, in Saturday’s quarter-final in Miami, and the German hailed his side.

“That is proper mentality. I’m very proud,” he said. “We needed everything. It was super difficult. In the moments we thought we catch the momentum, we had setbacks.”

On England’s reaction to their setbacks, Tuchel added: “This team really mean it. When the going gets tough, they never give up, they never lose belief. It was one step more.

“We need to take this in. This is Azteca, it’s Mexico, a crazy game. We left everything out there, every single one of us. We need to take this in, now it’s full steam ahead.”

England will almost certainly have to play the quarter-final without Henderson, who appeared to injure his wrist in a nasty fall during the celebrations.

News.title: England produce greatest World Cup victory since 1966
News.content:
We came to see England attempt to secure what would be the greatest win in their World Cup history outside their own island. This was it: the finest World Cup performance since 1966, and yet by the end it felt even bigger than that. An epic of which we shall talk about for years, a brilliant, resolute, flawed, 108 minutes in total of all the best of this thing we call English football.

First, that unbeaten Azteca Stadium record for Mexico in 26 competitive games going back to 2013: it’s over. It ended with the poor soul in the stadium address system having to press play on Three Lions at the final whistle and just short of 78,000 Mexicans forced to listen to “football’s coming home” and all that. It was not supposed to end like this for Mexico, but their World Cup is over. England face Norway in Miami on Saturday in a World Cup quarter-final.

They go with a lighter load than the burden shouldered by England teams of the past. For the first time in 40 years, the Azteca for England is no longer about Diego Maradona’s handball goal and then his great, humiliating second. Now, it is about this frankly absurd game which ended with England hurtling forward into the last eight of the World Cup, having turned up at 7,350 feet with no high-altitude preparation whatsoever.

To summarise this night: Jude Bellingham’s first-half goals, just 98 seconds apart, propelled England into a 2-0 lead before half-time. But by the time the break arrived, Julián Quiñones had scored for Mexico. In the 52nd minute, Jarell Quansah launched himself into Jesús Gallardo with the kind of red card-risk ferocity that even Donald Trump would struggle to get overturned on appeal.

News.title: How to protect your smartphone in a heatwave (and what to avoid)
News.content:
The UK and much of Europe have been experiencing record temperatures in recent months, and there is another heatwave predicted in parts of the country this week.

One of the more banal but irritating ways in which this persistent heat is affecting everyday life is by interfering with how you use your smartphone. If you’ve noticed your phone becoming too hot to handle or slowing down in the stifling heat, there’s a reason for that.

Here’s the full lowdown on why your phone is struggling in high temperatures, followed by some tips on what to do (and what not to do) with your handset when the heatwaves hit.

What’s the problem?

Put simply, phones do not like extreme heat. Both Apple and Samsung – the two biggest smartphone makers – state that their phones are designed to be used between 0C and 35C.

If a phone exceeds that maximum temperature, it will be forced to adjust its behaviour in ways that might affect your general use. Apple’s iPhones are known to dim their screens when things get toasty, which can prove counterproductive on sunny days.

You might also find that your phone gets slower due to so-called ‘throttling’. This is the term for when your phone’s internal chip reduces its processing speeds in an attempt to generate less heat.

News.title: ‘I apologise for the meltdowns’ says Djokovic after third-set tantrum
News.content:
Tell Novak Djokovic that time is the one opponent that cannot be beaten and he is likely to say, “Hold my jacket.”

Such is his aura, one can imagine him being wheeled on to Centre Court in his mid-80s, calculating that even on his worst days, his mere presence might make an opponent wilt under the formidable challenge of swatting him aside.

There he will be, still yelling expletives in his mother tongue, or smashing balls away after an untimely lapse in concentration, only to regain his composure to add to his Wimbledon win tally.

Roman Safiullin is the latest who can testify how it feels playing the legend rather than the ball. It has reached a point where most players must overcome the fear that beating Djokovic will jeopardise their chances of getting a signed photograph or post-match selfie with him.

You could be forgiven for thinking he teases awe-struck competitors, daring them to believe they have a chance, only to show off the extra gears he keeps in reserve.

News.title: Haaland dumps Brazil out of World Cup then leads Viking row celebrations
News.content:
A place in the World Cup quarter-finals is at stake in New Jersey as five-time world champions Brazil take on Norway at MetLife Stadium. These sides met during the group stages of the 1998 World Cup, with Norway winning 2-1. Brazil did in fact go 1-0 up that day in Marseille thanks to Bebeto’s goal but late goals from Tore Andre Flo and Kjetil Andre Rekdal led Norway to victory. Brazil had sealed top spot in Group A before that game as they went all the way to the final, where they lost to hosts France.

Norway’s current manager Stale Solbakken was in their playing squad during that World Cup and that was the last time Norway made the last 16 at the World Cup having failed to qualify in the six editions in between 1998 and 2026. The last time these nations met was back in 2006 in a friendly which ended in a 1-1 draw. Norway have in fact never lost to Brazil in four previous meetings.

Brazil topped Group C with two wins and a draw to earn a place in the Round of 32 against Japan. They fell 1-0 down in that game in Houston before coming from behind to win 2-1 with Gabriel Martinelli scoring a very late winner for Carlo Ancelotti’s side. The last time Brazil failed to make it past the last 16 at the World Cup was back at Italia 90, when they lost 1-0 to South American rivals Argentina at this stage of the competition. However, they have only made the semi-finals once since lifting the trophy in 2002.

“We are doing a good job,” Brazil boss Ancelotti said ahead of the game. “We are performing but you can never be content because we want to play better. We want to play at the highest level.”

Sports.title: Is Cristiano Ronaldo going to retire after the World Cup 2026?
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO’S final chance of securing World Cup success with Portugal has gone up in smoke.

The Portuguese icon has bagged three goals in this year’s competition.



PORTUGAL VS SPAIN LIVE UPDATES



Ronaldo, 41, scored two against Uzbekistan during a group stage encounter before bagging a crucial penalty to help Portugal beat Croatia in a tense round of 32 tie.

However, the footballing legend’s World Cup career has come to an end after seeing his side lose to Spain in the last-16.

Is Cristiano Ronaldo going to retire after the World Cup 2026?

Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed that the World Cup 2026 will be his last as a player – but he hasn’t ruled out continuing his career at club level.

Speaking in a press conference on Sunday, the Portuguese mogul said: “Let this be my last World Cup; it is my last World Cup, and I hope tomorrow won’t be my last match.”

Ronaldo previously refused to confirm whether the tournament would be his last even though he will be 45 years of age when the next competition rolls around in 2030.

He said: “I will finish when I choose. You always ask the same question: is this the last one? We will see. I don’t want to draw attention to this, the most important thing is to play well tomorrow,”

“I’m going to be perfectly honest, regardless of what happens tomorrow, Cristiano is going ⁠to be 1,000 per cent leaving with a clear conscience.

“I have given ⁠all I could to football, it’s my passion to play for so many years. I didn’t do it out of need, I’m doing well out of life. It’s about passion. I ‌play for the national team and I love to play football.



“Regardless of what happens tomorrow I’m not going to exert pressure on myself that I must win.

“You have to enjoy every match at a huge competition like the World Cup. I think I’m not ‌doing so bad. I’ve scored three goals, others have done better but I think I’m doing not so bad.”

Sports.title: Man City legends Bernardo Silva and Rodri in furious spat as heated Spain-Portugal clash turns stormy at World Cup
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY legends Bernardo Silva and Rodri were involved in an angry spat in the final seconds of their World Cup clash.

The two Premier League icons were facing off as Portugal lost 1-0 to Spain in their World Cup last-16 showdown.



With just moments to play, Silva had a chance which he narrowly headed over the crossbar.



Rodri then went up to his former City teammate and tapped him on the head.

But Portugal ace Silva was not happy with his friend toed foe, pointing an angry finger.

The two exchanged words, before the final whistle went just moments later.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s final World Cup clash ends in heartbreak as Portugal are dumped out by Spain
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO’S final World Cup clash ended in heartbreak as Portugal suffered a last-16 defeat to Spain.

The Manchester United legend, 41, revealed before the game this would be his last tournament.



But his dream of bowing out with the biggest trophy of them all was brutally ended when Arsenal star Mikel Merino scored a 90th-minute winner.



Ronaldo won the Euros with Portugal in 2016 and the Nations League in 2025 but never got his hands on the World Cup in a record SIX attempts.

Speaking before the match, he said: “It’s about enjoying it as much as possible.

“This will be my last World Cup, but let’s hope tomorrow isn’t my last game.”

Sadly for the footballing great, it was.

Ronaldo cut a shell-shocked figure at full-time as he stood on the pitch taking in his last international game.

The defeat means he will never equal his arch-rival Lionel Messi, who won the trophy in 2022 and could add to that tally this summer.

Sports.title: Portugal 0 Spain 1: Cristiano Ronaldo’s World Cup career OVER as Mikel Merino bags 91st minute winner
Sports.content:
SPAIN took the Mik-y with a last-gasp win which ended Cristiano Ronaldo’s World Cup quest.

A pretty tedious game was heading for extra time when substitute Mikel Merino grabbed the goal which put the lid on Ronaldo’s sixth and last finals.





It was a personal triumph for Spain boss Luis de la Fuente, whose decision to take off creative players Pedri and Olmo seemed to set the scene for more caginess.

Instead Merino combined with fellow substitutes Fabian Ruiz and Ferran Torres to send their team into the quarter finals.

Neutrals hoping for the most epic game for at least 18 hours were disappointed.

After the chaos and passion of Mexico City, two of the best teams in the world served up a lukewarm spectacle under the sterile roof in Arlington.

READ MORE WORLD CUP NEWS BET BOOSTER Best bet builder sites in the UK for 2026

Ronaldo, the first man to score in six tournaments, never looked like adding to his tally.

And fellow star attraction Lamine Yamal showed only flashes of what he could do.

So it was left to Spain’s supporting cast to take centre stage.

Although De La Fuente’s men were the better side in the first half and threatened to take control of the match at times, they could have found themselves behind at the break.



It looked ominous early on for Portugal when Pedri and Dani Olmo sliced them open with two quick passes. Mikel Oyarzabal ran through, only to send his shot wide of Diogo Costa’s left-hand post.

The Portugal ‘keeper had to make a double save not long afterwards. The first stop, from Yamal, was more for the cameras, but when Alex Baena sent the follow up curling towards the far corner, some Spanish reporters were already saying “si” in the press box.

Costa had other ideas, thrusting up a right hand to brilliant effect.

Then the ‘keeper cleared Pedri’s overhit cross with his left leg and should have been called up on again when Olmo sent the ball fizzing across the six-yard box.

Portugal were struggling by now to build anything from the back. Ronaldo was trying to get involved, sometimes dropping deep into his own half in search of something to do.



Then suddenly he came alive in the Spain box. Joao Felix’s header from Pedro Neto’s deep cross came off goalkeeper Unai Simon and Ronaldo improvised a flicked finish, only for Simon to dive full length to make the catch.

Moments later, Portugal worked a short corner and Pedro Porro channelled his inner Dan Burn to help Nuno Mendes’ fierce shot on to his own crossbar.

Portugal raised their level immediately after the break, with Neto looking threatening down the right.

But neither side seemed keen to overcommit in search of a win in normal time, so neither goalkeeper was troubled for a long spell.

Martinez sent on Rafael Leao for the ineffective Felix but it was Costa who made the first decent save of the half, from a Yamal free kick.



Fernandes hit the side netting, Ruben Dias blocked Olmo’s goalbound effort.

Yamal cutely played in substitute Ferran Torres but there was no-one in white to meet the cross.

De La Fuente’s next changes, taking off Olmo and Pedri, hardly set the pulse racing.

Yet replacements Ruiz and Merino combined to win the game.

Ruiz found Torres, whose reverse ball to Merino was lovely.



The Arsenal midfielder’s finish was the moment of quality the game had been waiting for.

Bernardo Silva headed on to the roof of the net in stoppage time and Joao Neves nodded wide at the death..

But they could not stop Ronaldo’s World Cup career ending in one last heartbreak.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a bit harsh’ – BBC ‘receive complaints over Danny Murphy’s Bob the Cat story’ during World Cup clash
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans complained to the BBC about Danny Murphy’s treatment of infamous cat Bob as the bizarre story got another chapter live on air.

The co-commentator has gone viral at the World Cup for anecdotes about his previous pet and gave another instalment during Portugal’s clash with Spain.





Talking to main caller Steve Bower during the first half hydration break, Murphy addressed yet more questions on his former cat.

Bower started: “Danny and I, in our last game, thought we had closed the story of Bob the cat.

“But again, the phones have not stopped bleeping so we must clear this up.

“There has been some complaint, Danny, about the seemingly hasty decision of yours to send Bob the cat to Preston.”



And Murphy replied: “It’s been a little bit unfair, a little bit harsh.

“Just to clarify, we did try and settle him back into the house.

“He started bullying and fighting his sister Mary so we made the decision to give him the red card and send him up the road to Preston.

“I think it was the right decision. I was between a rock and a hard place. What can I say?”

Bower responded: “I don’t think we need to say anymore. Although sister Mary is a new character in this story.

“Suffice to say it has created a lot of interest.”

Murphy could be heard muttering in the background: “Oh no. Oh boy.”

Ex-Liverpool man Murphy, 49, left many, including Bower, baffled during the group phase when he first revealed that his cat had been lost after jumping in a Royal Mail van and been driven away.

Murphy brought up the random fact during coverage of Norway attacker Oscar Bobb in their win against the Ivory Coast.



A dew days later, as Bower and Murphy were back together and Spain faced Austria, Murphy explained: “Well surprisingly Steve there was a lot of interest. But yeah he did not actually die.

“We did get him back six to eight weeks later but unfortunately he had gone feral and we could not re-integrate him into our home.

“And he ended up moving in with my friend’s parents in Preston and that was the life he had.

“He has since passed away unfortunately, many years ago. Thanks for all the concern to those who have been messaging us.”

The reaction from BBC viewers has been mixed with some unhappy with the lack of focus.



But others have enjoyed it.

One wrote on X after part three: “Danny Murphy has talked about a cat three times and he’s still been an easier listen than Lee Dixon“.

Sports.title: ‘I don’t get that vibe’ – Wayne Rooney worries Portugal stars may not like playing with Cristiano Ronaldo
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY does not believe Portugal stars enjoy playing with Cristiano Ronaldo in the same way Argentines do with Lionel Messi.

Ronaldo, 41, has started all five of Portugal‘s World Cup games thus far, scoring three goals.





But he is being outshone by a 39-year-old Messi who, with SEVEN goals in four games, is charging for the Golden Boot.

Messi is absolutely indispensable to Argentina but Rooney, who shared a Manchester United dressing room with Ronaldo for five seasons, does not get quite the same feeling when he looks at CR7 and Portugal.

The BBC pundit said: “You always put Ronaldo and Messi together because they are two of the best players the game has ever seen.

“But the Argentinian lads seem like they’re all there for Messi. They’re all behind him. Messi has obviously been fantastic at this World Cup.

“I don’t get that vibe from the Portuguese players.”

Some have even suggested that Portugal boss Roberto Martinez would be wise to drop Ronaldo – who is not as mobile as he used to be – for the good of the team.

The veteran forward was subbed in the 81st minute against Croatia in the last 32 before Goncalo Ramos, who started on the bench, bagged a late winner.

And even Rooney admits that more than two decades at the top level might be starting to catch up with his former team-mate.

He added: “We saw Erik ten Hag go against Ronaldo and the backlash that came with it.

“For Martinez it’s not just Ronaldo, it’s a legacy, it’s everything that goes with it.

“If I put myself in Martinez’s shoes, he has got to ask himself if he has any regrets, and I think he might do if he sticks with him.



“Sometimes age gets you and it looks like it has a little bit.”

Sports.title: Fans shocked as Cristiano Ronaldo’s fiancee Georgina Rodriguez sends gift to Lionel Messi’s wife in middle of World Cup
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO’S rivalry with Lionel Messi appears to have softened – after their Wags struck up an unlikely friendship.

The Portugal and Argentina superstars have spent their careers fighting for the title of football GOAT.





But their stunning other halves seem to be getting along just fine.

Antonela, 38, shared a picture on Instagram of a hamper full of yoga gear.

The Argentine captioned the post: “Thank you very much @georginagio.

“Everything is beautiful. I wish you all the success in the world.”

Georgina, who is Spanish but was born in Argentina, sent Messi’s wife what appears to be a yoga mat and some bags from her women’s activewear brand Mimoa.

Fans were shocked by the olive branch, with one writing: “Wow, this is lovely.”

Another said: “What a beautiful crossover!”

Although one cheeky fan joked it could be “witchcraft” while her husband leads Argentina at the World Cup.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

The pair have publicly supported each other in the past, often liking each other’s social media posts.

And while Ronaldo and Messi have spent the last two decades battling it out for the Ballon d’Or, the ex-Real Madrid star revealed there is no such rivalry off the pitch.

He said last year: “I have never had a bad relationship with Messi. It’s quite the opposite.”

Ronaldo revealed how 32-year-old model Georgina, who has her own Netflix show and is involved in a number of businesses, helped him in an awkward situation with an Argentine flight assistant during the World Cup.



The Manchester United legend, 41, said: “Many times in hotels, I’ve shared the lift with people who work there and the housekeeping, who are Latino.

“I said, ‘By the way you looked at me’. ‘How did I look at you?’

“I was joking, of course, and told her: ‘My partner is Argentinian. So obviously I have a special affection for Argentinians, too. She is from Buenos Aires.

“So it was all good, it wasn’t a problem!”

Sports.title: I fulfilled lifelong dream at World Cup but Mbappe left me thinking it will be impossible for England to win it
Sports.content:
THE WORLD CUP is magical and attending a match has been one of my lifelong dreams – like billions of football fanatics around the world.

But the fan experience was hammered from all corners before the tournament.





So I teamed up with Verizon to find out what the matchday experience is actually like for real fans and headed to France’s last-32 clash with Sweden at the New Jersey stadium where Kylian Mbappe ran riot.

England fans pay attention, because this is need to know info if the Three Lions get to the final!

The Journey and the ‘Soccer’ Culture Shock

A return train ticket from Manhattan will set you back $98 so as there were three of us we opted for a taxi which worked out around $70 each for a return.

Of course, it wouldn’t be America without a bit of a culture shock and I was immediately triggered by a roadside sign flashing the word “SOCCER”—come on guys, it’s football!



Arriving at the stadium, the wind was absolutely howling, doing zero favors for my hair. But the atmosphere quickly made up for it.

The sea of yellow Sweden fans was immense, though I did spot one brave bloke sporting an England shirt. Wrong game, mate!

And after what felt like a thousand-mile walk from the drop off point to the stadium, we finally made it through the security checks and into the external concourse which was absolutely mega.

That Magical First View

No matter how many grounds I visit around the world, there is one feeling that can never be matched: Walking up the stadium steps and seeing that vast green pitch for the very first time.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

It instantly took me back to 1997, being a little kid carried up the stairs at West Ham by my dad.

And I had that feeling again as I looked out at the vast arena, and felt the electricity in the air—nearly 30 years after my first ever experience of football, there is still absolutely nothing that beats it.

Filet Mignon and Pitchside Pints

Now, the Americans do a few things differently, and honestly? Some of it is brilliant.

For starters, you can buy a beer and drink it in full view of the pitch—a luxury we are denied in England. $20 for a lite lager though… hardly a bargain. And the food options are on another level.

I always thought The Sun’s head of sport Dean Scoggins was a “working-class man of the people,” until he ordered a filet mignon sandwich at $25 each!



Talk about posh nosh. But to be fair, it looked absolutely sensational and I couldn’t resist… Medium-rare, onions and mustard… Beautiful!

Before kick-off, the stadium presentation was superb. They rolled out whopping national flags across the pitch, which I love, and they really added to the sense of the grand occasion.

Then came the anthems. La Marseillaise is, without a shadow of a doubt, the best national anthem of the whole World Cup by a million miles. The stadium was absolutely buzzing and I even joined in!

Mbappe Runs Riot on a Narrow Pitch

Once the game kicked off, France showed their class, but the stadium layout threw up a minor annoyance.

Because it’s an NFL arena, the field is noticeably narrower than a traditional English pitch.



And because “soccer” pitches are wider, from where we were sitting, you could only see the nearside touchline if you stood up. But that’s being picky and it didn’t really affect my experience.

The arena is phenomenal as was the atmosphere. Apart from the bloke nearby who wouldn’t stop trying to force a Mexican wave!

But then, the magic happened. Mbappe picked up the ball on the left flank, cut inside onto his right foot, and curled an absolute beauty into the back of the net.

The Frenchman sprinted straight over to celebrate with manager Didier Deschamps who had only just flown back into camp after tragically losing his mother.



You could feel the unity in this French team—they were going through, no doubt about it.

At half-time, I asked some local American fans for their thoughts on hydration breaks.

Michael Aiello said: “They’re the silliest thing ever added to the World Cup. They completely ruin the flow of the game. You might as well just make it four quarters at that point and play American football!”

The second half was pure French dominance. Minutes after the restart, Michael Olise played a sublime ball through to Bradley Barcola, who slotted it home to make it 2-0. Game over, France through to the last-16.

VIP Access with Verizon

While the stadium erupted and a lone Norwegian fan did the iconic row in the stands, I chatted to Diego Cadena – one of many fans who won a Verizon Pitchside Access Golden Ticket through ticket drops and sweepstakes via the MyVerizon app.



Standing right down where the action happens, Diego was completely blown away by the experience:

He said: “This is the most surreal thing ever. It gives me goosebumps just thinking about it. Walking out right where the France team comes out is just insane.

“Being able to look around a packed stadium and sharing the same field as all these incredible players… as a kid growing up a soccer fan, you dream of being and playing on the biggest stage. Being able to experience this through Verizon is unreal.”

History in the Making

Back on the pitch, France were toying with the Swedes. Mbappe struck again to make it 3-0, putting on an absolute masterclass.

Watching him live, you get the distinct feeling you are witnessing history—one of the greatest players of all time doing his thing. It was impossible to think anyone other than France is going to win this tournament.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The final whistle blew on a flawless 3-0 victory for Les Bleus. What a day, what a performance, and what a tournament this is turning out to be.

It’s phenomenal once you get there, but make sure you leave plenty of time and with plenty of patience and cash in your pocket before heading to World Cup games. Then you’ll have the experience of your life.

‌

‌



Spain enjoyed the lions' share of possession and the better chances but were unable to translate that into a goal, while Nuno Mendes rattled the crossbar for Portugal after his ferocious strike from the angle of the penalty area ricocheted off a white shirt.

And it was Merino who popped up in the 91st minute to eliminate Portugal and Ronaldo, who confirmed this would be his final World Cup game just days ago.

Sports.title: Keir Starmer stepped in to stop FIFA moving England's World Cup kick-off over Mexico altitude fears
Sports.content:
Keir Starmer stepped in to stop FIFA moving England's World Cup kick-off over Mexico altitude fears

The UK Government stepped in to oppose FIFA moving the England vs Mexico match from 1am, fearing Thomas Tuchel's side would have less time to adapt to the altitude for their Round of 16 clash

View 2 Images England beat Mexico in Mexico City (Image: Richard Pelham, Getty Images)

Keir Starmer stepped in to stop FIFA from bringing forward kick-off at the Estadio Azteca, over fears the alteration could hand World Cup co-hosts Mexico an unfair edge over England.

‌



The UK Government intervened through diplomatic means to block moving the fixture from 1am to 7pm BST because it would mean Thomas Tuchel's squad had less time to acclimatise to the altitude, it is understood. Starmer ordered the intervention after being made aware of the potential issue by the Football Association, which is understood to have contacted Downing Street ahead of the match.

‌



England battled past hostility, altitude and Jarell Quansah's red card to clinch a thrilling 3-2 victory against Mexico on Monday morning UK time and secure a quarter-final showdown with Norway.

‌



View 2 Images Starmer stepped in over fears Mexico would get an unfair advantage by moving the kick-off time (Image: DAN KITWOOD, POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

The fixture was scheduled to kick-off at 1am UK time (6pm local time), but with the risk of lightning in the vicinity, the stadium implemented its thunderstorm protocol and the game eventually began at 2am UK time (7pm local time).

‌



Outgoing Prime Minister Starmer intervened last week with emergency legislation to permit pubs to remain open late for the Round of 16 tie.

England went on to beat Mexico 3-2 in one of the Three Lions' most thrilling performances in recent memory. Thomas Tuchel’s belief that England can win the World Cup was fuelled by the win – but the night also increased his concerns about the potential for “erratic” officiating costing his side.

Those who stayed up late to watch the delayed last-16 encounter on an electrifying evening at the Estadio Azteca were rewarded with an inspirational performance against adversity.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson shows true colours after horror England injury as World Cup plan emerges
Sports.content:
Jordan Henderson shows true colours after horror England injury as World Cup plan emerges

England midfielder Jordan Henderson suffered a serious arm injury as the team celebrated their World Cup Round of 16 win over Mexico at the Azteca Stadium

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson suffered an arm injury following a fall after England's win over Mexico

It's hard not to feel a huge degree of sympathy for Jordan Henderson following the freak injury he sustained during England's iconic post-match celebrations after beating Mexico in their own backyard.

‌



The expectation is that he will miss the remainder of the World Cup with a suspected broken arm following a bizarre accident where he slipped and fell while attempting to leap over the advertising boards at the Azteca Stadium.

‌



If Henderson's career and achievements are anything to go by, he will be kicking himself because this is likely his last World Cup.

‌



But equally, the 36-year-old's importance to the group and this particular England team should not be understated.

Gianni Infantino breaks silence on Folarin Balogun decision after Donald Trump bombshell READ MORE :

Jordan Henderson leaves on stretcher with oxygen after freak injury in England celebrations READ MORE :

It's why news that Henderson, fitness permitting, would ideally like to return to camp to support his colleagues will be well received. Not only that but it reflects the veteran's true character and his humility to put others before himself.

He might not be everyone's favourite footballer but you will struggle to find a player of his professionalism and alongside Harry Kane, he sets the standard for the rest of the England team to follow.

‌



After a horrific moment and ordeal like that, you could understand if Henderson might want to return home to be with his family.

Yes, it's not an ACL or broken leg but it must weigh heavily given England were in the midst of celebrating such a special achievement and night.

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson picked up an injury after England's 3-2 win over Mexico (Image: Martín Fonseca/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



It speaks volumes that Henderson was actually the first player to run onto the field from the bench to celebrate with his teammates.

He kicks every ball from the sidelines and that's why he's on two yellow cards at this tournament despite only playing six minutes at this World Cup.

Thomas Tuchel was also subdued in his press conference because he was upset about the incident and the fact it looked poised to deny Henderson the chance to continue competing at this World Cup.

‌



The Three Lions need to keep him around the group because he keeps everyone grounded and that's why it's a big relief, though unsurprising, to hear Henderson's No.1 priority is to return to camp and still play some kind of role for this team.

He looks destined to become a coach and this experience may potentially give him a firm taste of what life might be like on the other side of the white line.

Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe hits out at 'despicable' and 'brazen' racist abuse from politician after France beat Paraguay

The row after France's win over Paraguay continues to boil over as Kylian Mbappe responds to racist abuse from a Paraguayan senator

France star Kylian Mbappe has slammed Paraguayan senator Celeste Amarilla as 'despicable and unworthy' of her position following a vile racial outburst on social media. The Real Madrid star scored the only goal in Les Bleus' 1-0 win over the South American side in the Round of 16.

‌



The ill-tempered game saw Didier Deschamps' side scrape through an ugly encounter which saw the Paraguayans miraculously escape without a yellow card despite some senseless challenges on the World Cup favourites. France will play Morocco in the quarter-finals, but the fallout from Thursday's encounter continues.

‌



Amarilla is a senator of Paraguay's Liberal Radical Party and the government figure hasn't hidden her anger after Paraguay's exit. The 61-year-old has launched a vile tirade on social media with a series of social media posts aiming vitriolic abuse towards Mbappe with foul language and racial undertones.

‌



Belgium to make last-ditch Folarin Balogun challenge after FIFA throw out legal appeal READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino breaks silence on Folarin Balogun decision after Donald Trump bombshell READ MORE :

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Days after France's progression with their focus on a place in the semi-final of another World Cup, Mbappe spoke out against Amarilla. He said in a tweet: "Madame Celeste Amarilla, you are a despicable woman and unworthy of your position.

"You do not represent Paraguay, that country which has sweated passion and honour throughout the competition. Through your recklessness and your brazen racism, the entire world has already forgotten the journey and the historic effort that your players accomplished during this World Cup, making way for an incompetent woman who gives the worst possible image of her country.

‌



"I will never allow people like her the freedom to spread their hatred and racism across the world."

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe was targeted by the Paraguayan defenders during their Round of 16 battle. (Image: Getty Images)

The French Football Federation condemned Amarilla's comments, describing them as "utterly abhorrent and unacceptable" and said they would refer them to the public prosecutor's office with a view to legal proceedings.

‌



In a tweet, they said: "The racist remarks made by Paraguayan Senator Celeste Amarilla targeting Kylian Mbappé are utterly abhorrent and unacceptable. How can anyone make such comments? These remarks are criminal and deserve condemnation. They must be prosecuted, here and elsewhere. The FFF is referring the matter to the public prosecutor's office with a view to legal proceedings.

"The Federation offers its full support to its captain, its players and, more broadly, to all victims of such hateful remarks. More than ever, the FFF remains committed to fighting racism and all forms of discrimination. These comments bring shame on those who make them and those who spread them. The players of the French national team represent France, it is our country that has been insulted.

"It appears that Amarilla's social media activity against Mbappe isn't an isolated incident, as she warned not to let her into the stadium, as she threatened to turn into a hardcore fan before expressing disdain towards the footballer."

‌



The aftermath of the ugly encounter in New York has filtered into the media with accusations from Deschamps that he was subjected to insults following the win.

Meanwhile, former Paraguay goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert sparked a race row ahead of the game after remarking that the tournament favourites are a 'squad from Africa'.

French football federation president, Philippe Diallo, has since condemned the claim from the 60-year-old ex-shot-stopper.

Article continues below

Diallo said on social media: "I condemn in the strongest possible terms the racist remarks made by José Luis Chilavert against the French national team, which undermine the values of respect, fraternity, and diversity in our football.

"If he was once a great goalkeeper, this man has now fallen into disgrace."

Sports.title: England fans reflect on magical night in Mexico as they flock to Miami for Norway showdown
Sports.content:
England fans reflect on magical night in Mexico as they flock to Miami for Norway showdown

Now... Miami! England supporters are still reeling from an incredible game at the Azteca stadium against Mexico in the World Cup Round of 16, and are now heading to Florida

View 5 Images England fans in Mexico City (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

England fans have woken up this morning in Mexico City and are still celebrating one of the most magical games in the country’s football history.

‌



As they went for breakfast, they were still taking in the sensational performance of Thomas Tuchel’s heroic ten men. But there wasn’t much time for them to rest on their laurels. Some were at the airport for the 6.50am AeroMexico direct flight to Miami ready for the next World Cup adventure on Saturday.

‌



manchester-city-fc>Manchester City’s Erling Haaland awaits, and the fantastic army of Norwegian fans complete with their brilliant rowing routine which has wowed the world. Others were flying back home to England for work reasons but are returning to Miami on Friday.

‌



View 5 Images England fans gave amazing support (Image: World Cup 2026 News Pool (WCNP))

Gianni Infantino breaks silence on Folarin Balogun decision after Donald Trump bombshell READ MORE :

Trump admits not knowing what a red card was before Balogun sending off as Ted Cruz thanks him for FIFA call READ MORE :

Over breakfasts in hotels and restaurants, Three Lions supporters were still taking in enormity and impact of the win. Many said it was their “best game ever”. Older fans said it would never beat the 5-1 win over Germany in Munich in 2001.

But there was no doubt it was one of the most dramatic and sensational matches in England’s history. Superfan Gary Taylor was at the match with girlfriend Jo Lewis.

‌



View 5 Images England players celebrate with fans after game (Image: World Cup 2026 News Pool (WCNP))

He said: “Fair play to the Mexico fans they were great in defeat.” Gary and Jo had a horrendous experience at the opening ceremony in Mexico City last month when they were caught in a crush.

“It was so much different this time,” he said. "What a match - that ranks in my top three games of all-time. It doesn’t beat Germany away in 2001, and 2002 World Cup against Argentina, but it was just fantastic. It was a real privilege to be here.”

‌



The country’s most dedicated fan, Tony Incenzo, who has visited every single non-league ground in the National League pyramid - more than 2,500 of them - said: “I’ve been watching the World Cup since 1970 and that was one of the best matches I’ve ever seen.”

View 5 Images Great spirit between England and Mexico fans (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

The big scramble for tickets was underway last night. On the official FIFA resale site one ticket was available at £7,000. On Seatgeek there are several available with price ranging from £2,200 to £3,000. Incredibly one cheeky punter has his ticket on sale for £5.6m.

‌



Businessman Dan Fellows, 37, originally from Wolverhampton, now lives in Houston, Texas. He has followed England across the country this summer, attending most of their matches so far, and already has tickets for the semi-final and final. With his flight and hotel booked for Miami, all that's missing is a quarter-final ticket.

View 5 Images Harry Kane hugs Peter Crouch after the game (Image: World Cup 2026 News Pool (WCNP))

He said: "A World Cup quarter-final in Miami — it doesn't get much better than that. I've been to nearly every England game this tournament, and I've already got my tickets for the semi and the final. Now I just need one for Saturday, but I'm pretty confident I'll get one.

Article continues below

"Watching it on TV is one thing, but being there in person - the atmosphere, the noise, thousands of England fans singing — it's something you have to experience for yourself." The Wolves fan added: "What a great chance we've got against Norway. I can't wait”

Miami will see thousands of new England fans descending from the UK. But many have been in Florida for a while - using it as base to watch the games on big screens rather than incur travel and ticket costs.

The match will be played at the Miami Stadium; home of the legendary Miami Dolphins NFL team. It has a capacity for 64,000 fans.

Sports.title: 'I thought I was done!' - Menzies bounces back with title
Sports.content:
Cameron Menzies claimed his first title of the year at Players Championship 23, defeating Cristo Reyes 8-5 in Monday's final.

The Scotsman, who had previously won two ProTour titles in Leicester back in 2024 and 2025, emerged through a 128-player field to take the £15,000 top prize at the Mattioli Arena.

The 37-year-old's triumph also came with an added bonus by confirming his spot at the Betfred World Matchplay, which takes place in Blackpool later this month.

"It's been a tough year, I was lucky… I think I needed that because I have struggled this year," conceded Menzies, who spoke honestly about his tribulations following an emotional day in Leicester.

Menzies made headlines at the World Darts Championship in December when he punched a table following an opening-round defeat, an incident that left him needing hospital treatment after seriously injuring his hand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies furiously smashed the water table with his fist after suffering a dramatic 3-2 defeat to Charlie Manby at the World Darts Championship.

He continued: "I never thought I'd win one of these again! I thought I was done, I made a mistake - I let my family and my friends down. It's a moment that I have to accept.

"I genuinely thought [my] darts were spiralling because I was struggling. It hasn't been my best performance, to even get to the quarter-finals I was buzzing - I think I've won one board final all year!

"I'm in a good place in life at the moment, when your home life is good - [your] darts are good," expressed Menzies, who opened up on the benefits of having a life coach alongside the support he has received from back home.

The Blackpool-bound Scot began the afternoon with an impressive whitewash victory over Carl Sneyd - averaging north of 102 in the process.

Menzies then went on to beat Nathan Potter before winning another contest without reply, this time against Norway's Cor Dekker.

From there, the Scottish star picked up a statement victory over Josh Rock, winning six straight legs to beat the Northern Irishman 6-3.

The World Cup semi-finalist then got the better of Charlie Manby before completing another thrilling comeback victory against Dave Chisnall to book his place in the final.

After enjoying a successful start to the contest, Menzies blew multiple chances to extend his lead to 4-1 over the Spaniard. Reyes eventually broke the Scotsman's throw with a 20-darter - which momentarily got him back into the game.

Image: Cameron Menzies claimed his first title of 2026

However, Menzies responded brilliantly by winning legs in 12, 15 and 12 darts again to extend his lead to 6-2.

In a game of twists and turns, Reyes went on to reel off three legs on the spin before a ten-darter from Menzies - which put the Scot one leg away from the crown in the East Midlands.

From there, the Ayrshire ace took care of business - sealing an 8-5 victory over Reyes to win his first ranking title of 2026.

Elsewhere, Joe Cullen produced perfection in his clash against Jack Tweddell, although his exploits came in a losing cause, as Tweddell ran out a 6-3 winner against the former Masters champion.

The 2026 ProTour season continues tomorrow afternoon in Leicester as the race to qualify for the Betfred World Matchplay continues, with the likes of Damon Heta and Daryl Gurney fighting to confirm their spots whilst others remain in the hunt.

Sports.title: Fery's fairy-tale Wimbledon run continues as Brit reaches quarter-finals
Sports.content:
Arthur Fery - Britain's last remaining hope in singles - kept his Wimbledon dream alive as he sealed a sensational five-set victory against Grigor Dimitrov to reach the quarter-finals.

Fery, who will climb inside the ATP top 100, was aiming to become the first British wild card, man or woman, to reach the quarter-finals at a Grand Slam in the Open Era.

He edged out 35-year-old Dimitrov - a 2014 semi-finalist at the All England Club - 7-5 3-6 4-6 6-4 7-6 (10-7) in a classic encounter on Centre Court.

"Where to start? I have no words right now. I'll do my best. It's incredibly difficult to put words to what I just felt on a tennis court. The support was phenomenal," Fery said on Centre Court.

"First time on this court, five sets against an absolute legend of the game. I grew up five minutes from here. I grew up coming to watch matches on this court."

He added: "We've got probably the greatest of all time watching from the front row [Roger Federer]. And now playing here in front of all you guys, having the support, and winning, it's unbelievable."

Who is British tennis star Arthur Fery?

Born in Sevres, France, Fery grew up in London and attended King's College School in Wimbledon.



Tennis is in his blood. Fery's mother, Olivia Fery (née Gravereaux), was a former player on the WTA Tour and played at the French Open in the early '90s.



His father, Loic Fery, is the current president at FC Lorient, who compete in the French Ligue 1.



Fery went to Stanford University, where he majored in Science, Technology and Society, as well as becoming one of the best tennis players in the country.



Fery played main-draw doubles at Wimbledon in 2021 and 2022 before winning his first main-draw match at Wimbledon in 2025 and then sealing his first Challenger singles title in Barranquilla.



The 23-year-old qualified for the Miami Open and reached the semi-finals of the Zagreb Challenger before the start of the grass-court season where he made the semi-finals at the Birmingham Open and then secured his first ATP 500 quarter-final at Queen's Club.



Fery is coached by Benoit Foucher and Jeroen Benard.



The 23-year-old entered the tournament as a wild card ranked 114, with only two Grand Slam victories to his name and never having won a five-set match.

Now he has won two in a row, both from seemingly hopeless positions, after beating the Bulgarian big-hitter.

After all the doom and gloom surrounding British tennis to start the fortnight, Fery's run has been quite the plot twist, and the Centre Court crowd roared on their new hero.

"It's been the story of the tournament for me. I was really close to losing my last round as well," Fery added. "Just trying to keep fighting, keep trying to have a good attitude.

"I'm playing really well with my back against the wall and it paid off today.

"I couldn't have imagined it," he added. "Now winning four matches, being in the quarters, it's a dream of mine."

His victory makes him the first British wild card to reach the quarter-finals at a grand slam in the open era, while he joins Andy Murray, Tim Henman, Cameron Norrie, Roger Taylor and Greg Rusedski as home male members of the Wimbledon last-eight club.

Did you know...

Fery is the first player ranked outside the top 100 to reach the last eight of the men's singles at Wimbledon since No 144 Nick Kyrgios in 2014.



He is currently up to world No 63 in the ATP Live Rankings.



Fery turns 24 on men's finals day - July 12.



The last wild card to win a Grand Slam title was Goran Ivanisevic at Wimbledon in 2001 - 25 years ago.



Tale of the Tape: Dimitrov vs Fery

Fery to face Cobolli in quarter-finals

Image: Flavio Cobolli joked that he needed a house to live in for the rest of Wimbledon after beating Alex de Minaur to reach the quarter-finals

Cobolli kept his cool to book another quarter-final spot with victory over Alex De Minaur and joked his father must book a longer stay in London next year.

The popular Cobolli delighted the Court One crowd in hot conditions with an array of eye-catching shots and failed to let two stoppages for spectators to receive treatment knock him off his stride on his way to a 7-5 7-6 (7-4) 6-3 victory.

French Open runner-up Cobolli offered his own water to one member of the crowd and later asked during his on-court interview if anyone had a spare room after the tenancy on the house he lived in for week one of the Championships ended.

Cobolli, who is cheering for Portugal in the World Cup, said: "My grandfather helped us to find a solution for tonight, but we found solution for all the week, I hope.

"An Italian family gave us all the house here in Wimbledon, so it's really cool. I will say thanks to them when I see them."

He later added: "Today I found a way to have a high level for, I don't know how much I played, but for all the match. I'm proud and happy ​to reach a second quarter-final in a row here at Wimbledon. That means a lot for me.

"I played for my first time here on Court One. The feeling on the court was incredible. I love to play there. The sound was amazing and amazing feeling with the ball."

Eala's dream run comes to an end

Image: Jasmine Paolini (left) hugs Alex Eala after winning in three sets

Jasmine Paolini ended the dream Wimbledon run of Alexandra Eala and dashed the hopes of a nation.

Eala's march to the fourth round, after her shock victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, had captured the imagination of almost the entire 120 million population of the Philippines.

Sports arenas around the country hosted watch parties for thousands of supporters to cheer on the 21-year-old, who had broken new ground for her nation just by winning a match here.

But the parties ultimately fell flat as it was 13th seed Paolini, watched by Formula One star and fellow Italian Kimi Antonelli, who steered her way into the quarter-finals after a 6-4 4-6 6-3 win.

Sports.title: Fury vs AJ could be at Wembley with later start time
Sports.content:
The blockbuster heavyweight clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could still be held at Wembley Stadium, but only if local authorities agree to stage the fight at a later time than usual.

Turki Alalshikh, who is organising the all-British bout, said on Monday that he wants the fight to take place at a time that works for a global audience, and intends to hold talks with the London Mayor Sir Sadiq Khan in a bid to obtain permission to host a late-night fight in the capital.

Given main events at UK bouts tend to start somewhere between 10pm and 11pm, Alalshikh would appear to be suggesting the much-anticipated matchup would start after midnight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Groves admits it's difficult to pick a clear winner between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua but believes Oleksandr Usyk's influence on AJ should not be underestimated.

Speaking at an event in London, Alalshikh said: "I tell you from the beginning, it depends if England give us all that we need, we want the fight here in England.

"But we want the time zone of all the world, especially in America. If they allowed us to have Wembley late in the night, we want to do it in England. It is about the time and viewership.

"We will talk with the mayors and Prince Abdullah (bin Khaled bin Sultan)."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Promoter Frank Warren provides the latest on what's happening regarding Tyson Fury's potential fight with Anthony Joshua.

Both of the former world champions are competing in warm-up fights later in July, with a surprise defeat or injury for either appearing to be the only potential obstacles to their meeting going ahead, most likely in November.

Fury faces Mariusz Wach in Thailand on July 24, while Joshua is taking on Kristian Prenga a day later in Saudi Arabia.

Sports.title: Joyce misses out on heavyweight title shot as Gassiev opponent confirmed
Sports.content:
Murat Gassiev's first defence of his WBA heavyweight title will go ahead on Saturday after a replacement opponent was found for the Russian.

Gassiev, who was elevated from regular to full WBA champion status after Oleksandr Usyk vacated the belt last month, had been scheduled to face Tony Yoka before the Frenchman dropped out with a back injury.

After speculation that Britain's Joe Joyce, who is also fighting on the IBA Pro 19 bill in Moscow, could get a title opportunity, Germany's Peter Kadiru has ultimately been given the opportunity to face Gassiev.

Gassiev, who holds a 33-2 professional record with 26 knockouts, said: "I was fully prepared and ready for Tony Yoka, but boxing is unpredictable and champions must adapt.

"Peter Kadiru is a big, strong, experienced fighter with a solid amateur pedigree and real power. Fighting at home in Moscow in front of my Russian fans for my first defence is special."

Image: Murat Gassiev defends his WBA heavyweight title for the first time

Kadiru holds a 23-1 record, having amassed nine successive victories since the sole defeat of his professional career in 2022.

The most recent of those was a unanimous decision victory over Senad Gashi in May.

Kadiru said: "Since my win over Senad Gashi, I've been in the gym training and wanting to be back in the ring. I'm excited for the opportunity to travel to Russia and challenge for the WBA Heavyweight World Title on July 11.

"This is my moment. My team and I are locked in and Moscow should get ready for a big performance."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gassiev's promoter Al Siesta is confident his fighter would beat Moses Itauma and states he'll unify the heavyweight division in the next two years

Joyce, who fights Artem Suslenkov on the undercard, had been touted as a potential opponent for Gassiev, but misses out on a world title shot.

The 40-year-old has lost four of his last five fights and faces a dangerous opponent in the unbeaten Suslenkov.

The division was blown wide open by Usyk vacating his WBC, WBA and IBF titles in June, despite the Ukrainian insisting he has not retired from the sport.

Britain's Daniel Dubois holds the WBO title that also previously belonged to Usyk, while Agit Kabayel has inherited the WBC belt.

Sports.title: Portugal 0-1 Spain: World Cup 2026 last 16 – live reaction
Sports.content:
now 17.07 EDT Spain are delighted. They settled a faintly dreadful match with some quick-thinking right at the end of the 90 minutes. Ferran Torres with the cute ball down the channel, Mikel Merino with the calm slot home. As Spain hug each other in a mixture of joy and relief, the Portugal players stare at various points in the middle distance, only just coming to terms with the fact that there won’t be any extra time. Cristiano Ronaldo stands awhile, hands on hips, holding off the tears … but he’s on the verge of breaking. This one will hit hard. It’s over. Spain meanwhile will face either the USA or Belgium in the quarters on Saturday! Share

5m ago 17.03 EDT FULL TIME: Portugal 0-1 Spain Spain are through to the quarter finals! Portugal are out, and Cristiano Ronaldo’s World Cup career comes to a sudden end! 5m ago 17.02 EDT 90 min +9: Fernandes swings the free kick in. Neves throws himself at the ball, but misses, and the ball goes out for a goal kick. And that is surely that! Share

6m ago 17.02 EDT 90 min +8: Iglesias comes on for Oyarzabal. Then Torres slides in reckessly on Conceicao. A daft free kick to concede, and a yellow card. Costa comes up for the free kick, which will be sent in by Fernandes. Share

7m ago 17.01 EDT 90 min +7: In the aftermath of that miss, Silva is furious with his old Manchester City team-mate Rodri, and goes looking for a fight. Simon intervenes and stops Silva from doing something daft. Share

8m ago 17.00 EDT 90 min +6: Conceicao curls a delicious cross in from the right. Silva rises above Rodri and from six yards out, should score, but guides his attempted header towards the top left over the bar! A huge opportunity to force extra time goes by! Share

10m ago 16.58 EDT 90 min +5: Leao crosses from the left. Cubarsi cushions a calm header into the road of Ruiz, who belts clear. Time really not on Portugal’s side now, though there should be a couple of extra minutes added on for the goal celebrations and other assorted cavorting. Share

11m ago 16.56 EDT 90 min +3: Leao probes down the left, but there’s no pass on. Ronaldo skips around in irritation, demanding a ball he’s never getting. Yamal breaks back up the flank, and he’s cynically clipped by Semedo, who goes into the book. Share

13m ago 16.55 EDT 90 min +2: Ronaldo looks pig sick, irritated with his defence switching off. You can’t really blame him, they were caught daydreaming while Spain got on with things quicksmart! Share

14m ago 16.54 EDT GOAL! Portugal 0-1 Spain (Merino 90+1) Rodri is fouled 40 yards out. The free kick’s taken quickly, Portugal snoozing. Torres slips a ball down the inside-left channel, releasing Merino, who slots low and hard into the bottom left, six seconds into stoppage time!
